svg.text: 2048 WebApp: secure CI/CD delivery on AWS
Push to GitHub, Jenkins builds, tests and scans, image goes to ECR, ECS Fargate runs it behind a load balancer
VPC 10.0.0.0/16 with Flow Logs on, spread over two Availability Zones
Public subnet A (AZ A): only the NAT gateway and load balancer are public
One NAT today to save cost.
Regional NAT is the resilience option.
The only public entry point to the app. SG-alb allows HTTP 80 from the internet.
Forwards to healthy tasks on port 8080. Health check path is /health.
HTTPS with an ACM certificate is listed as a planned improvement.
No public IP, private subnet only
Admin access through SSM, not SSH
Instance role, no stored AWS keys
6 Push to ECR, 7 Deploy to ECS
Read-only root filesystem, tmp volume for nginx
All Linux capabilities dropped, no privilege escalation
No public IP, logs sent with the awslogs driver
Auto scaling 2 to 6 tasks on requests and CPU
Minimum 2 tasks, one per AZ, even when idle
Rolling update, circuit breaker rolls back bad deploys
Second AZ keeps the game up if AZ A fails
Task execution role: pull from ECR, write logs
Task role: empty, the game needs no AWS access
SG-app: inbound only from the load balancer
Outbound goes through NAT (ECR and CloudWatch)
Only task execution role can pull
Log group /ecs/2048 with 30 day retention, KMS encrypted
VPC Flow Logs for network audit
Alarms: unhealthy targets, ALB 5xx errors, task CPU high
Cross-cutting controls used by everything above
Jenkins instance role: push to one ECR repo, update one ECS service
Task execution role: pull image, write logs
Task role: empty, no AWS permissions
No IAM users and no access keys anywhere
Encrypts ECR, logs, EBS and alarms
Key policy limits who can use it
S3 bucket: versioned, own KMS key
How a code change reaches production
Jenkins polls GitHub every 2 minutes from its private subnet, through the NAT gateway.
Pipeline runs: lint, build image, test the container, scan with Trivy.
Only if every check passes, the image is pushed to ECR with the commit SHA as tag.
Jenkins updates the ECS service and waits for it to become stable, or rolls back.
Fargate tasks pull the image from ECR using the task execution role.
Users reach the game over the internet through the load balancer, the only public door.
The load balancer sends traffic only to healthy tasks, on port 8080.
Tasks send logs to CloudWatch. VPC Flow Logs record network activity.
CloudWatch alarms notify you through SNS when something is unhealthy.
